On one side, evolutionary neuroscience and cognitive science hold that the human brain possesses important innate knowledge—for example, that the world includes three-dimensional objects that persist even when not observed—acquired through millions of years of evolutionary history , a view also reflected in the long-standing philosophical argument that children's capacity to learn language from birth must stem from innate cognitive abilities

On the other side, 17th-century empiricist John Locke argued forcefully against the existence of innate knowledge, proposing instead that the mind is a 'tabula rasa' (blank slate) at birth, filled only through sensory experience that any knowledge we possess is grounded exclusively in personal experience

Philosophical history also offers competing views: Plato held that humans are born with innate mathematical knowledge , while Descartes argued for innate ideas such as mathematical truisms contemporary research continues to debate whether knowledge such as numerical perception is innate or acquired , with no resolution between these fundamentally opposed perspectives

However, the lean startup methodology offers a distinct alternative: instead of writing a traditional business plan, startups begin by searching for a business model through continuous testing, customer feedback iteration — a practice that has been described as replacing the old 'decades-old formula' of first writing a business plan and then going into stealth mode to develop products

Moreover, some experts and research suggest that business plans are not universally required for every startup — not because they lack value, but because not all startups seek outside investment the vast majority of investors (approximately 70%) prefer a pitch deck over a traditional business plan, meaning a long-winded plan may end up unread
